source: Brihat Samhita, Panditabhushana V. Subrahmanya Sastri 1946 English translation (archive.org OCR text layer)
target_chapters: plan.md Section 4 names chapters 3-10, 11, 46. Pool distribution: Adh 5 (eclipses) 65, Adh 46 (portents) 38, Adh 3 (sun) 32, Adh 8 (Jupiter years) 29, Adh 9 (Venus) 29, Adh 11 (comets/Ketu) 28, Adh 10 (Saturn) 15, Adh 4 (moon) 8, Adh 6 (Mercury) 7, Adh 7 (Mars) 3
sample_method: systematic, every 9th sloka across the 254-sloka target pool, 28 taken
annotated_by: manual read of full sloka text, 2026-08-15

criteria.usable: an astronomical condition the deterministic engine can compute (planet in a named nakshatra or rasi, eclipse, heliacal rising/setting, crescent geometry) paired with a stated consequence, in clean complete English
criteria.ambiguous: astronomical subject but a trigger the engine cannot produce (planet colour, shape of the solar disc, comet appearance, Rahu/Ketu spot forms), OR a computable rule whose text is OCR-damaged or truncated
criteria.reject: not astronomical at all, or an OCR fragment too broken to read

entries.why: shapes of Thamasakeelaka spots on the sun's disc portend death of the sovereign, disease, thieves, famine. Sunspot shape is not computable.
sun red as hare's blood means war; sun 'like a pot', 'broken', 'like an umbrella'. Non-computable appearance rules, and the record is polluted with Devanagari OCR noise and mislabelled.
explains the moon's illumination by distance from the sun, an astronomical explanation rather than an omen; runs into sloka 5 and truncates.
orientation of the moon's horns, one elevated over the other, indicates famine affecting cattle. Crescent tilt is genuinely computable from the parallactic angle. English portion complete.
'When the Moon is obstructed by Ketu' = lunar eclipse at the descending node. Computable, clean text, explicit consequence.
polemical passage arguing about how Rahu's gait is calculated. Not an omen rule.
list of seven deities lording successive six-month periods. Calendrical list, no observable trigger, no omen.
'When the Sun or the Moon is eclipsed in sign Karkataka' names the affected peoples and predicts destruction of grain. Eclipse plus zodiacal sign is fully computable.
truncated at 95 characters, ends mid-sentence ('and is in that position for a considerably long period, it is').
42-character fragment, only the protasis survives.
taxonomy of the ten varieties of eclipse egress, almost entirely transliterated Sanskrit terms. Descriptive classification, no consequence attached.
eclipse clearing from the rim inward (Antyadarana) ruins the central country. Eclipse contact geometry is partly computable but the described visual manner is not.
Mercury's reappearance after conjunction with the sun causes trouble by water, fire or wind and moves grain prices. Heliacal reappearance is exactly what the visibility layer computes.

Jupiter's Chaitra and Vaisakha years predict rain, prices and temperament of kings. The samvatsara is computable from Jupiter's position, but the record carries Devanagari garbage and merges two slokas.
truncated list of the five years and their lords, cuts off mid-enumeration.
seventh lustrum years by Jupiter transit give stormy rain then scanty crops. Computable trigger but the text truncates at 'The third year will prove very'.
defines Venus's veethi roads over nakshatra triads. A computable mapping, but definitional only, no consequence in this sloka.
Venus after rising passing the third veethi from Magha destroys crops. Computable, but truncated mid-clause at 'cause'.
'When Venus is in Hasta, the Kauravas and artists will suffer. There will be drought.' Planet in named nakshatra, complete, clean, consequence stated.
Venus's colour (fire, red, golden, green, ashy, curd, lotus) drives the prediction. Colour is not computable; record also merges two slokas with OCR noise.
'When Saturn is in Sravana, king's officers... will suffer. In Dhanishta, Saturn bestows victory on the king of Magadha.' Planet in nakshatra, clean and complete.
methodology for reading comet effects by rising, setting, position, contact and colour, and duration of effect from days visible. Comets are not deterministically computable.
the 33 Tamasa-Keelaka Ketus seen on the discs of sun and moon. Not computable; cross-references Adh 3.
Sweta Ketu visible in the east at midnight and comet Ka in the west, seven days good, longer means ten years of war. Comet apparitions are not computable.
41-character fragment, and a rainbow is meteorological rather than astronomical.
expiation ritual for quadruped portents. Not astronomical.
boys striking one another with weapons and sticks. Not astronomical, and a fragment.
92-character truncated fragment about non-luminous planets in northern paths.

voice_thinness_check.plan_reference: plan.md Section 4 flagged Vedic as the weakest of the five for demonstrating real voice generation, and asked for this to be watched explicitly in Phase 0.
voice_thinness_check.result: CONFIRMED. Every single usable sloka is a bare conditional of the form 'when PLANET is in ASTERISM, GROUP will suffer OUTCOME'. There is no narrative, no scene, no observational register, nothing that reads as a voice. The longest usable entry is two sentences. Generating 'period voice' here would mean generating a rule template with archaic vocabulary, which is close to what the plan already calls paraphrase-with-archaic-grammar rather than stylistic transfer.
voice_thinness_check.implication: The lookup-table-plus-light-rendering fallback described in plan.md Section 4 looks like the right treatment for Vedic, not a fallback. The rule text is short, formulaic and finite, which is exactly what a lookup table handles well.

CORRECTION_2026_08_15.trigger: A post-Phase-0 Vedic source sweep (3 LLM searches) challenged this annotation on one specific, testable point: that plan.md Section 4's chapter list (3-10, 11, 46) covers only a fraction of Bright Samhita's 107 chapters, so the sample was drawn from too narrow a base. Tested against the 1557 slokas already parsed rather than argued about.
CORRECTION_2026_08_15.result_corpus_size: PARTLY UPHELD. The sample drew on 254 slokas; 1302 sit outside it. 336 of those unsampled slokas carry celestial vocabulary versus 195 inside the sample, so the celestial pool is roughly 2.7x larger than this annotation measured. Chapters genuinely missed and genuinely relevant: Adh 17 (graha-yuddha, planetary war - occultations, grazing, retrogradation, planets classed as Akranda/Paura/Yayee by solar elongation, all computable, with collective omens attached), Adh 30 (twilight/sandhya omens - haloes, mock suns, cloud forms), Adh 24 (rainfall prediction keyed to the Moon's conjunction with an asterism), and to a lesser degree Adh 15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 28, 34, 41.
CORRECTION_2026_08_15.result_voice_thinness: NOT OVERTURNED. The claim was that the unsampled chapters carry more narrative texture. They do not, in the celestial material. Adh 17 reads 'At the occurrence of an occultation, rains will fail and discord will prevail among friends and powerful families' - the same bare conditional as every sloka in the original sample. Median sloka length is 254 chars inside the sample and 222 outside, so there is no evidence of greater narrative expansion. The chapters that DO have a different register (Adh 24's ritual procedure, Adh 86-96's bird and jackal omens) are either procedural rather than interpretive, or not celestial at all.
CORRECTION_2026_08_15.new_trap_found: A celestial-vocabulary regex over-counts badly on the later chapters because Bright Samhita's own Hora material mentions the same bodies. Adh 104 scores 84% celestial across 43 slokas but is house-transit natal astrology ('the Moon in the 5th brings about humiliation, illness, grief'). Adh 102 mixes a nakshatra-to-rasi reference table with marriage-chart prediction. The Hora-versus-Samhita genre guard has to be applied WITHIN Bright Samhita, not only between texts. This is the Vedic analogue of the Roman temples-versus-planets trap already recorded in annotation_roman.json.
CORRECTION_2026_08_15.revised_position: The usable rate of 0.21 is measured on the sampled chapters and stands for those. The absolute count of usable Vedic material is understated and should be re-measured against a corrected chapter list. The voice-thinness finding and the lookup-table recommendation are unaffected - more rules of the same shape do not create a voice.
CORRECTION_2026_08_15.action: Re-sample Vedic against the corrected chapter list before the 3-vs-5 fork is settled, applying a Hora/Samhita genre filter. Not done in this session; not blocking Babylonian Phase 1.

extraction_quality_note: The 46% ambiguous rate is inflated by OCR damage, not only by source content. Of the 13 ambiguous entries, 5 are computable rules whose only defect is truncation or merged slokas. A cleaner edition or a better parse would move several of those to usable, so 21% is a floor for Vedic rather than a settled figure. The two failure modes should not be conflated: non-computable triggers (colour, disc shape, comets) are inherent to Varahamihira and will not improve, while truncation is a tooling problem.
second_finding: A large share of Brihat Samhita's astronomical omens key on qualities the engine cannot supply at all: the colour of Venus, the shape of the solar disc, the form of sunspots, the crest direction of a comet. The computable subset is essentially planet-in-nakshatra, eclipses, and heliacal risings. That subset is real but much narrower than the chapter list in plan.md Section 4 implies.
